title: Relation as Part of the Codec
compression: Shared relational history can supply side information for conceptual decompression.
source_reconstruction: In sustained collaboration, compact messages may depend on accumulated shared vocabulary, examples, corrections, and interaction expectations that are not explicitly restated in each message.
assumption_envelope: Meaning may depend partly on shared context outside the immediate message.
Greater compression can increase decoder-mismatch risk.
Shared context does not make every interpretation correct.
decoder_prerequisites: Distinguish the explicit message from side information available to the decoder.
Distinguish conversational familiarity from epistemic warrant.
candidate_invariants: A message can become shorter when decoders share relevant prior context.
Transfer can fail when the message survives but the shared decoding context does not.
cliffs: Do not confuse familiarity with truth.
Do not assume a future decoder shares the same relational context merely because it receives the same tokens.
